pages.text: "Give me that!" Mina, a handspan shorter than Raju, pulled at a wooden doll. The river was so low that the yard tub held the whole family's water today. Beside it, experienced eldest Raju hid the doll behind their back.
"I want to play with it, too!" Mina stamped. Raju shook their head, doll still behind them. "I took it out first." Mina's hands slowly rose to Raju's shoulders.
Both hands shoved. Raju staggered back, a toe knocking the tub. It tipped, pouring water out.
The yard soil drank it all. The tub was empty. Both children were soaked to their toes. The doll fell into a muddy pool.
Mom stood the tub upright. "Raju, are you all right? Mina, pushing can hurt. Tell us what you want." They looked at each other.
Mina spoke first. "Sorry I pushed. I wanted to try, too." Raju picked the doll from the mud and wiped it on their clothes. "Then count to ten, and we'll switch."
After Mina counted ten, Raju handed it over. "Don't Push—Say It!" Sitting together, they stood the doll up. It walked over dry soil.
At the bottom step, Mom tilted the empty tub into the water. From the higher step, Mina and Raju held its rim together. Their towel-dried backs were already dry and soft.
Back in the yard, they played again. When Mina's turn ended, Raju held out a hand. "Mine now." Mina passed the doll.
Mom drew both close at her sides. Mina told Raju, "Next time, I'll ask with words."
